qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Massive scale in Medicaid and ACA marketplace administration (~28M members, ~$195B revenue) provides provider network contracting advantages, but returns are structurally bounded by government-mandated reimbursement rates, statutory minimum medical loss ratio floors (85%), and acute exposure to medical cost trend shocks.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & zero autonomous pricing power, REJECT). Centene operates as a massive scale government-sponsored managed care contractor, but structural returns on capital hover at 3-8% (10Y median 8.5%), failing the 12% hurdle. Premiums are set administratively by state Medicaid agencies and CMS, leaving margins vulnerable to medical inflation, utilization spikes, and post-redetermination acuity mismatches.
qualitative.evidence: Centene generates ~$195B in top-line revenue but operates at razor-thin margins (~1.9% operating margin in 2023-2024, swinging into operating losses in 2025 due to utilization spikes and goodwill impairments). 10-year median ROIC of 8.5% fails the 12% hurdle. Total debt stands at ~$17.4B with cash/investments held primarily at regulated insurance subsidiaries. Centene lacks autonomous pricing power: state Medicaid budgets dictate premium rates with significant actuarial lag relative to medical trend spikes.
